name: Gail Pellerin
title: California State Assemblymember, Chair of the Assembly Elections Committee
district: California State Assembly District 28 (roughly half of Santa Cruz County and part of Santa Clara County, including the city of Santa Cruz, Scotts Valley, and part of San Jose/Morgan Hill)
years_of_service: December 5, 2022 to present. Pellerin was elected in November 2022 and re-elected in November 2024; her current term ends December 7, 2026, and she is running for re-election in 2026.
background: Pellerin holds a B.S. in Journalism (1984) from California Polytechnic State University, San Luis Obispo. Before entering elections administration she worked as a campaign assistant, a newspaper reporter and photographer, and a community college instructor. (Source: official Assembly biography, a28.asmdc.org, via cached page text, and California Commission on the Status of Women and Girls profile, women.ca.gov/gail-pellerin.)

Pellerin worked in the Santa Cruz County elections department for 27 years beginning in 1993, and served as the elected Santa Cruz County Clerk and Registrar of Voters from 2004 until her retirement in December 2020, running unopposed in her re-election contests. She was President of the California Association of Clerks and Election Officials (2010 to 2012), co-chaired the California Secretary of State's Voting Accessibility Advisory Committee, and served twice as an international election observer in Nagorno-Karabakh (2015 and 2017). (Source: Wikipedia, Gail Pellerin, used because Ballotpedia's page on Pellerin could not be retrieved despite repeated attempts; and women.ca.gov/gail-pellerin.)

Pellerin was elected to the California State Assembly in November 2022 for the newly configured District 28, placing first in the June 2022 top-two primary with 35.9% of the vote and defeating Republican Liz Lawler 68.0% to 32.0% in the general election. She was re-elected in November 2024, again defeating Lawler, 66.9% to 33.1%. Drawing on her election-administration background, she chairs the Assembly Elections Committee and, on arriving in Sacramento, requested creation of a select committee on the state's mental health crisis, on which she is now vice chair. (Source: Wikipedia, Gail Pellerin; Santa Cruz Sentinel, "State Assemblymember Gail Pellerin running for second term," Nov. 1, 2023.)

voting_record_highlights: AB 1784 (2023 to 2024), permitting primary-election candidates to withdraw their nomination documents and clarifying that a candidate cannot run for more than one office at the same election: Pellerin was the lead author, introduced as chair of the Assembly Elections Committee. It passed the Assembly concurrence vote 62 to 0 on August 22, 2024, and was signed by Gov. Gavin Newsom on September 22, 2024 as Chapter 355, Statutes of 2024. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status and bill text for AB 1784.)

AB 2839 (2023 to 2024), the Protecting Democracy from Deepfake Deception Act, restricting the distribution of materially deceptive AI-generated election-related media: Pellerin was the lead author. It passed the Assembly concurrence-in-Senate-amendments vote (with urgency clause) 63 to 8 on August 30, 2024, and was signed by Gov. Newsom on September 17, 2024 as Chapter 262, Statutes of 2024. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for AB 2839; her office's fact sheet, pellerin.asmdc.org.)

AB 1267 (2025 to 2026), banning marriage for anyone under 18 with no exceptions: Pellerin is the lead author. It passed the Senate unanimously and the Assembly concurred in Senate amendments 78 to 0 on August 26, 2026; it was enrolled and presented to Gov. Newsom on September 3, 2026 and, as of this profile's retrieval date (September 22, 2026), has not yet been signed. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status and bill text for AB 1267.)

SB 42 (2025 to 2026), the California Fair Elections Act of 2026: Pellerin was one of six Assembly principal coauthors (with Assemblymembers Berman, Kalra, Lee and Senators Becker, Blakespear, and Stern) on the Senate bill. Gov. Newsom signed it October 2, 2025 as Chapter 245, Statutes of 2025, placing the measure before voters as Proposition 4 on the November 2026 ballot. Full detail on the measure itself is covered in content/measures/ca-prop-4-2026.json and is not duplicated here. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for SB 42.)
attendance: No individually published floor-attendance or voting-participation record for Assemblymember Pellerin was found. The California State Assembly does not publish a per-member attendance scorecard; the only public records are bill-by-bill roll-call votes at leginfo.legislature.ca.gov, which is what the voting-record entries above are drawn from. Digital Democracy (CalMatters) tracks bill-passage counts and interest-group vote-alignment percentages for legislators generally but was not confirmed to include an attendance metric for Pellerin specifically.
